title: Q4 2025 earnings: RAPIDe-3 readout reaffirmed, commercial build underway
haeExtract: Management reaffirmed RAPIDe-3 topline guidance for Q3 2026. Cash position of approximately $280M reported as sufficient runway through launch preparation. Commentary positioned deucrictibant as a 'continuum-of-care' oral asset across on-demand and prophylaxis (illustrative). Analyst questions focused on launch timing and mechanism differentiation versus oral kallikrein inhibitors.

title: Q4 2025 earnings: HAE cited as cornerstone rare disease franchise
haeExtract: HAE cited among top-5 growth contributors in the rare disease segment. No new pipeline announcements for HAE. Commentary focused on patient services, geographic expansion, and real-world evidence generation. Oral-modality threat framed as 'segment addition rather than substitution' (illustrative).

title: Q4 2025 earnings: Orladeyo exceeds $440M; CCO transition announced
haeExtract: Orladeyo 2025 revenue of approximately $445M reported (illustrative), growth moderating as early-adopter conversion matures. CCO transition announced. Pediatric Phase III and extended-release Phase I advancing per plan. Management positioned oral modality as 'the future of HAE management across the continuum' (illustrative).

title: Investor Day: rare disease strategy emphasis
haeExtract: HAE franchise positioned as a durable growth contributor through lifecycle management. Executive commentary framed oral entrants as expanding the overall HAE market rather than taking share from Takhzyro. Commitment to continued investment in real-world evidence and patient services (illustrative).

title: Pharvaris initiated at Outperform; $42 price target
haeExtract: Analyst highlights deucrictibant dual-indication value and estimates peak sales of approximately $900M across on-demand and prophylaxis programs (illustrative). Identifies RAPIDe-3 readout as the defining catalyst. Flags Pharvaris as a potential acquisition target for a larger rare disease franchise holder.

title: Q3 2025 earnings: RAPIDe-3 enrollment completion, commercial hiring signals
haeExtract: Full enrollment of RAPIDe-3 confirmed. Commercial hiring activity disclosed in prepared remarks, including US medical affairs buildout. First mention of ex-US manufacturing partnership process underway (illustrative).

title: BioCryst: Orladeyo growth moderating; watch for next oral catalyst
haeExtract: Analyst notes deceleration in net-new patient adds for Orladeyo and flags the extended-release program and pediatric label as key upside drivers. Views BioCryst as less exposed to oral on-demand competitive pressure than incumbents with SC portfolios.

title: Takeda rare disease: HAE defense scenarios
haeExtract: Analyst models three scenarios for Takhzyro post-sebetralstat launch: defensive hold (base case, 5 to 10% share loss over 3 years), moderate erosion (15 to 20%), and aggressive displacement (25%+). Highlights patient services investment as the most credible defensive lever.

title: Q2 2025 earnings: extended-release program announced
haeExtract: Management announced next-generation oral plasma kallikrein inhibitor (extended-release formulation) with Phase I initiation targeted for Q4 2025. First explicit signal of lifecycle strategy to address single-daily-dose limitations of Orladeyo (illustrative).

title: R&D Day: pipeline focus on oral-modality leadership
haeExtract: Strategic framing centered on 'owning oral prophylaxis' in HAE. Pediatric, extended-release, and geographic expansion called out as three growth vectors. No announcement of on-demand program consideration (illustrative).

title: Pharvaris Q4 2025 digest: RAPIDe-3 timeline reaffirmed, commercial scale-up accelerates
haeExtract: RAPIDe-3 readout reaffirmed for Q3 2026, with rolling filing planned under Fast Track designation. Management framed deucrictibant as a 'continuum-of-care' asset across on-demand and prophylaxis. Commercial hiring pace suggests a US launch in H2 2027 if data are positive — the 18 to 24 month sebetralstat first-mover window remains intact but tightening (illustrative).

signal.label: PIPELINE SIGNAL
signal.text: Management's reaffirmation of Q3 2026 readout timing, combined with 'continuum-of-care' positioning across on-demand and prophylaxis, signals a broader commercial strategy than initially indicated. The 18–24 month sebetralstat first-mover window remains intact but is tightening.

implications.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR EKTERLY
implications.text: Pharvaris' accelerating commercial build and maintained RAPIDe-3 timeline suggest launch preparation is on track for H2 2027. This preserves Ekterly's prophylaxis positioning window but sharpens competitive urgency. Fast Track designation for rolling filing could compress the timeline further if data are strong.

quotes.text: We're building the commercial infrastructure now — US medical affairs, KOL engagement, market access groundwork — so we're ready the moment data read out.
Deucrictibant as a continuum-of-care asset — patients on demand therapy today who want to step up to prophylaxis — that's the story we're telling.

title: BioCryst Q4 2025 digest: Orladeyo growth moderates, pediatric and extended-release are next acts
haeExtract: Orladeyo annual revenue exceeded $440M with year-over-year growth moderating as early-adopter conversion matures. Management leaned into pediatric Phase III progress and the next-generation extended-release program as future growth vectors. Tone on oral on-demand entrants remained constructive — framed as market expansion, not substitution (illustrative).

signal.label: GROWTH SIGNAL
signal.text: Orladeyo growth moderation to +12% YoY reflects early-adopter saturation in the US prophylaxis market. CCO transition creates a brief strategic uncertainty window. Extended-release program initiation signals BioCryst is investing in lifecycle management rather than defending current share alone.

implications.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR EKTERLY
implications.text: Moderating Orladeyo growth is a relative positive for Ekterly's on-demand positioning — the prophylaxis market is maturing and acute therapy remains the largest unmet need. CCO transition introduces a brief window of reduced commercial pressure from BioCryst, which Ekterly should leverage for HCP engagement.

quotes.text: We view oral modality as the future of HAE management — from on-demand through to prophylaxis — and we intend to own that continuum.

title: Takeda Q4 2025 digest: HAE reaffirmed as core franchise, no oral-modality move signalled
haeExtract: Management cited HAE among top-5 growth contributors in rare disease and reaffirmed franchise commitment. No pipeline announcement of oral on-demand work. Defensive strategy continues to lean on Takhzyro real-world evidence and patient services, not new clinical mechanisms (illustrative). Q&A focused on competitive readiness rather than R&D pivots.

signal.label: COMPETITIVE SIGNAL
signal.text: Takeda's consistent framing of oral entrants as 'market expansion rather than substitution', combined with zero pipeline announcements for oral HAE, confirms their defensive strategy centres entirely on patient services and real-world evidence — not platform innovation.

implications.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR EKTERLY
implications.text: Takeda's continued RWE investment strengthens Takhzyro's moat among established patients. However, the absence of any oral-modality response leaves new-diagnosis patients open for capture. New HAE diagnoses not yet started on prophylaxis represent the primary market expansion opportunity for Ekterly's on-demand positioning.

quotes.text: Oral entrants are expanding the overall HAE market — patients who previously went untreated now have accessible options. We don't see this as competitive displacement.
quotes.attribution: EVP Rare Disease, Takeda Q4 2025 earnings call (illustrative).
